hints.title: Two jobs at once
hints.body: Lookups must be fast, and recency order must be updated quickly. A plain array or a plain sorted list makes one of those jobs expensive.

hints.title: Combine a map with a linked list
hints.body: A hash map finds nodes in constant time. A doubly linked list keeps recency order, with the most recent node at one end and the least recent at the other.

hints.title: Move on access
hints.body: On a hit or an update, unlink the node and put it at the most-recent end. On an insert into a full cache, remove the least-recent node before adding the new one.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
cache = map from key to node
recency = doubly linked list, most recent at front
for each operation:
    if get:
        if key is absent: record -1
        else: move node to front; record its value
    else:
        if key exists: update value and move node to front
        else:
            if size == capacity: remove the node at the back
            insert a new node at the front
return the recorded get results
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution.
